title: Part 1: Profile badge progress, clickable leaderboard modals, games played column, paginated match history

requirements.summary: Display all badge definitions in Profile tab with progress indicators for unearned badges
acceptanceCriteria: Profile tab shows all badge definitions, both earned and unearned
Unearned badges display a percentage progress bar
Unearned badges display a count label such as '3/10 wins'
Earned badges are visually distinct from unearned ones
Progress is computed from the user's existing stats/match history data

file_operations.description: Modify ProfileBadges to display all badge definitions (not just earned ones). For each badge, compute progress from userStats and matchHistory data. Show earned badges in full color and unearned badges dimmed with an overlaid progress bar and count label (e.g., '3/10 wins'). Add helper functions to calculate current progress for each BadgeCriteria type (totalWins, winsStreak, totalGamesPlayed, etc.) from the user's stats and history.

Create a utility module for badge progress calculation. Export a function computeBadgeProgress(definition: BadgeDefinition, stats: T | null, matchHistory: DayWithLog[]): { current: number; required: number; percentage: number } that handles all BadgeCriteria variants and returns current progress, required threshold, and percentage. Handle edge cases (null stats, empty history) gracefully.

requirements.summary: Make leaderboard player rows clickable to open a profile modal with chart, streaks, and badges
acceptanceCriteria: Each player row in the leaderboard is clickable
Clicking opens a modal (not a page navigation)
Modal shows a bar chart of the selected player's wins and losses over time
Modal shows the selected player's current win streak and best win streak
Modal shows all badges earned by the selected player
Modal can be dismissed to return to the leaderboard

file_operations.description: Make each player row in the leaderboard table clickable. Add an onClick handler that opens a PlayerProfileModal component, passing the selected player's principal. Use cursor-pointer and hover styles to indicate clickability.

Create a modal dialog component that displays a selected player's profile. Accept a principal prop and an onClose callback. Fetch the player's stats (via getUserStats), match history (via a new hook), and earned badges (via getUserBadges). Display: (1) a bar chart of wins/losses over time using the ProfileWinLossChart pattern, (2) current and best win streaks computed from match history, (3) earned badges grid using the ProfileBadges pattern. Use shadcn/ui Dialog for the modal overlay. Show loading state while fetching data.

Add a new React Query hook useGetUserMatchHistory(userPrincipal: Principal | null) that fetches match history for any user (not just the caller). This hook should call a backend method if one exists; if not, return an empty array for now (we'll handle backend in Part 2 or later). Ensure the hook is disabled when userPrincipal is null.

requirements.summary: Add 'Games Played' column to the Leaderboard table
acceptanceCriteria: Leaderboard table includes a 'Games Played' column
Value is calculated as wins + losses for each player
Column is visible alongside existing wins, losses, win %, and streak columns

file_operations.description: Add a new 'Games Played' column to the leaderboard table. Compute the value as (wins + losses) from each player's stats. Insert the column between the existing columns in a logical position (e.g., after 'Losses' and before 'Win %'). Update table headers and cell rendering accordingly.

requirements.summary: Replace the 5-entry match history limit with full pagination in Profile tab
acceptanceCriteria: Match history in the Profile tab shows more than 5 entries
Pagination controls (next/previous or page numbers) allow browsing all records
Each page shows a reasonable fixed number of entries (e.g., 10 per page)
Loading state is shown while fetching additional records

file_operations.description: Replace the current 5-entry limit with client-side pagination. Display 10 entries per page. Add pagination controls (prev/next buttons or page numbers) below the match history list. Maintain the current loading skeleton and error handling. If the full match history is already fetched via useGetCallerAvailableDaysWithLogs, slice it by page; otherwise, consider a paginated query hook for better performance in the future.
